name: get_rig
description: The skeleton being edited: its bones (parent, length, setup pose), slots (a picture's slot also gives its image, size in pixels, pivot pixel, and where that pivot is in skeleton space with its world rotation: pixel (u, v) of an unturned picture is at at + (u - pivot[0], pivot[1] - v)), IK constraints, the library's pictures, skins, animations and frame rate, and which animation, frame and skins the editor shows. Call this first. Values use Spine's conventions: x right, y UP, rotation in degrees counter-clockwise, all local to the parent bone.

name: get_animation
description: Every key of one animation, per bone: frame, local x, y, rotation, scaleX, scaleY and the ease of the interval that starts at the key (with `eases` for properties that follow their own). Also its length in frames, whether it loops, and whether it is a cycle (its last frame is frame 0 again); for a cycle, `seam` lists every bone whose pose at that last frame differs from frame 0, where the loop would hitch. Keys set by other tools (constraints, meshes, events) are not listed.

name: get_pose
description: Where bones are at one frame, as the Spine runtime poses them (IK and every constraint applied): each bone's world position (y up), world rotation in degrees and world scale. Use it to check an edit, e.g. that a foot touches the ground (y near 0 for most rigs).

animation.description: Animation name; omit for the setup pose.

name: new_animation
description: Create an empty animation. It loops over `frames` frames: frame `frames` is the same instant as frame 0, so a looping animation keys the same pose at 0 and at `frames`.

frames.description: Length in frames at the rig's frame rate.

name: set_keys
description: Key bones at frames, all in ONE undoable step. Each key sets any of x, y, rotation, scaleX, scaleY (local to the parent bone, Spine conventions: y up, degrees counter-clockwise; absolute values, not offsets from setup); what a key leaves out keeps the value the animation already has at that frame. `ease` shapes the motion from this key to the next: linear (default), hold, in, out, inout, or a cubic bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2] in 0..1. `eases` gives single properties their own ease over the same interval, e.g. {"y": "out"} for a ball that travels x linearly and slows in y; it replaces the key's earlier per-property eases ({} clears them), and `ease` given alone clears them too. Keying past the end lengthens the animation.

name: delete_keys
description: Remove keys, in one undoable step. A bone left with no keys goes back to its setup pose in that animation.

name: show
description: Show an animation at a frame in the editor, so the user sees it (the stage, the timeline and the Preview follow). `skins` picks which of the rig's skins (get_rig lists them) are shown, combined over the default skin; [] shows the default skin only. Choosing skins is one undoable step.

name: undo
description: Undo the last steps, whoever made them (each tool call that edits is one step). Returns what was undone.

name: redo
description: Redo steps undone.

name: check_preview
description: Play the animation in the real Spine runtime (the Preview panel, what a game will show) at the given frames and compare every bone with the editor's pose. Returns the largest difference in pixels; anything above 0.01 means the file would not play as the editor shows it. Needs the Preview panel open. For a cycle it also reports `seam`: the bones whose last frame does not match frame 0.

name: get_reference
description: The animation's reference: pictures the user added to animate against, frame by frame (get_rig lists which animations have one). Returns how its images sit in time (which frames each shows) and in the skeleton's space (where an image pixel lands), and the images at the frames you ask for, at most 6 at a time. Look at the reference's key poses before keying.

frames.description: Frames whose reference image to return. Omit to get only the timing and placement.

name: render_frame
description: A picture of the skeleton at a frame (omit animation for the setup pose: what add_bones and attach built), drawn as the editor's stage draws it, over the reference image at that frame (half transparent) when there is one, with every bone drawn as a line from its joint to its tip and named: blue for bones named far or right, magenta for the rest. Also returns each bone's joint and tip in the picture's pixels, and how a pixel maps to the skeleton's space. Use it to compare your pose with the reference and to see what you made; fix what does not match with set_keys and look again. With `paths`, each named bone's tip is also drawn at every frame, joined into its path, the keyed frames as rings: an arc you can judge in one picture.

animation.description: Animation name; omit for the setup pose.

reference.description: Draw the reference behind the skeleton (default true).

bones.description: Draw and name the bones (default true).

paths.description: Bones whose path to draw: where the bone's tip is at every frame of the animation (needs animation).

name: add_bones
description: Create bones in the setup pose, all in ONE undoable step. Give each bone its joint `from` and its tip `to` in skeleton space (y up: the space get_pose and render_frame report), or its local x, y, rotation and length under its parent (Spine conventions). A parent is an existing bone or one earlier in the list; omit it for a root. Names must be new. render_frame and get_reference say how a pixel maps to skeleton space, for reading joints off a picture.

to.description: Tip [x, y] in skeleton space: the bone's direction and length.

name: attach
description: Put pictures on bones, all in ONE undoable step: each becomes a slot that moves with its bone. `image` names a library picture (get_rig lists them with their sizes) and adds it; `layer` names artwork already in the skeleton (a slot get_rig lists, e.g. from File ▸ Import PSD as Layers) and moves it onto the bone, staying where it is. `pivot` is the pixel of the picture (from its top-left) it turns about, usually the joint: for a layer it moves only that point, not the artwork. For an image, `at` is where the pivot pixel goes in skeleton space (default: the bone's joint); `rotation` turns the picture counter-clockwise in the world (default 0: upright, as drawn). A new picture draws in front of what the bone already holds; draw_order changes that.

layer.description: Artwork already in the skeleton, to move onto the bone.

name.description: The new slot's name (default: the image's).

pivot.description: [u, v] in the picture's pixels from its top-left (a new image: default its centre; a layer: default unchanged).

at.description: [x, y] in skeleton space (default the bone's joint).

name: add_ik
description: Add an IK constraint in one undoable step: `bone` reaches for `target`. A bone whose parent is a bone gets the two-bone solve (the parent turns too: a shin reaching for a foot target turns the thigh); a root bone only aims. Without `target`, a target bone <bone>_target is made at the bone's tip. Key the TARGET to animate the limb: the bones the IK turns must never be keyed, so a bone with keys is refused (delete_keys first). `bendPositive` picks which way the joint bends (default true); flip it if render_frame shows the knee or elbow bent backwards.

target.description: An existing bone outside the chain; omit to make one.

name: auto_rig
description: Build a whole skeleton from a character's joints, in ONE undoable step: bones named hips, torso, head, thigh_near, shin_near, foot_near, upper_arm_near, forearm_near, hand_near… (near/far for a side view, left/right for a front view), each picture layer that is on no bone put on the bone running through it with its joint as the pivot, the drawing order kept as the layers were stacked, and IK on the legs (and arms with armIk). To read the joints: render_frame with no animation shows the pictures and how a pixel maps to skeleton space; give each joint where the body bends, in skeleton space (y up). pelvis and neck are required; a limb stops at its first missing joint (hip defaults to pelvis). Returns which layer went on which bone; look with render_frame and fix what is off with attach, or undo and run it again.

joints.description: [x, y] per joint: pelvis, chest (where the ribcage starts, when the pelvis and torso are drawn apart), neck, head (top of the head), and per side (side view: .near and .far; front view: .left and .right, as on screen) shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand (fingertips), hip, knee, ankle, toe. E.g. {"pelvis": [0, 100], "neck": [0, 160], "knee.near": [8, 52]}.

facing.description: A side view's facing (default right): which way a straight knee or elbow will bend.

layers.description: The picture layers to rig; default every one on no bone.

armIk.description: IK on the arms too (default false: arms are keyed by their bones).

name: list_motions
description: The motion library: ready-made clips (walk, run, idle, jump, and front-view ones) that apply_motion fits onto this rig, each with the body roles it moves (thigh.near, shin.near, upperArm.far, torso, head, hips…), and the roles guessed for this rig's bones from their names, for side-view and front-view clips.

name: apply_motion
description: Make a new animation from a library clip, fitted to this rig, in ONE undoable step: each role's limb points the way the clip says (so any proportions and setup pose take it), the feet stay on the ground, and limbs under IK get their targets keyed instead of their bones. Side-view clips face right; `facing: "left"` mirrors them. Roles are guessed from bone names (list_motions shows the guess); `map` overrides roles ({"thigh.near": "leg_l_up"}, or null to leave one out). Returns the mapping it used and a check of the result against the runtime pose; then refine it with set_keys like any animation. The animation is a cycle (see set_cycle).

animation.description: The new animation's name (default: the clip's).

map.description: Role → bone name, over the guess.

facing.description: Which way the character faces (side-view clips). Default right.

frames.description: Length in frames; default the clip's length at the rig's frame rate. Longer is slower.

name: draw_order
description: Reorder what draws in front, in one undoable step: the listed children of `parent` (bones and slots; omit parent for the skeleton's roots) draw in this order, FRONT first, in the places they held; the others keep theirs. A bone carries everything below it, so the near arm goes in front of the torso by ordering the chest's children, e.g. ["arm_near_up", "torso", "arm_far_up"].

name: key_draw_order
description: Key the draw order at a frame of an animation, in one undoable step: from that frame on (until the next draw order key) the listed layers draw in this order, FRONT first, in the places they hold there; the others keep theirs. A bone stands for the pictures hanging directly on it. `setup: true` instead keys a return to the setup order. Spine's draw order keys; get_animation's `drawOrder` lists them.

front.description: Layer or bone names, front first.

name: key_ik
description: Key an IK constraint's mix, bend and softness at a frame of an animation, in one undoable step (Spine's IK keys). From the key on the mix tweens to the next key by `ease` (linear by default; stepped holds; smooth eases in and out) and the bend is the key's until the next key. Before the first key the constraint's own mix and bend hold. A mix of 0 lets the chain bones play their own keys (FK); 1 is full IK. `bendPositive` has add_ik's sense: flip it to bend the knee or elbow the other way from that frame on. Leaving mix, bendPositive or softness out keys the value in force there. `delete: true` removes the key at that frame. get_animation's `ik` lists the keys.

ik.description: The constraint's name, as get_rig lists it.

softness.description: Pixels: near full reach a two-bone chain eases into straight over this distance instead of snapping. Tweens with the mix.

name: set_cycle
description: Make an animation a cycle, or let it play once. A cycle loops with its last frame showing frame 0 again: an animation that did not end that way grows by one frame for it, and every bone that reaches the end without a key there gets frame 0's pose keyed at that frame. Turning it off only stops the looping; keys stay. One undoable step. get_animation's `seam` then lists any bone that still does not close.

name: get_bone_path
description: Where a bone's tip (or origin) is at every frame of an animation, in the skeleton's space as get_pose reports it (y up), as the runtime poses it (IK included), with the frames where the bone itself has a key. Dots far apart mean fast, close together slow. A cycle's path stops before its last frame (it is frame 0 again) and is `closed`.

name: set_bone_path
description: Key where a bone is (x, y local to its parent, y up, as set_keys) at frames, and bend the path between consecutive keys with Bezier handles: `out` on a key is the handle leaving it, `in` the handle arriving at it, both points in the same space as x, y. The bend is written as the x and y eases of the interval (no extra keys), so Spine plays it exactly; where an axis does not move between two keys and has to bend, a key is added in the middle of the interval. An interval without handles is left as it is. Not for a bone the IK moves: key its target. One undoable step.

in.description: Handle arriving at this key, [x, y].
